advances: Exact two-law bound for a fixed proper planar affine profile with a nontrivial bounded centered branch.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use the centered cone energy records 18e7bdf54588779d and the bounded-cone-laws result f4be2679c83c2fd1, both with $d=2$ and the same $H$. For cone layers put $e=C/C_0$, $q=M/C_0$ and let $v$ be the probability of $b\le1$ under the uniform law of $b$ on $[-s,s]$ (at $s=0$, $\delta_0$). Integrating the energy and using $q=-(1-a)\partial_a e/2$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
0\le s\le1:\quad&
v=1,\quad e=(1-a^2s^2)^{-1},\quad q=-\frac{(1-a)as^2}{(1-a^2s^2)^2},\\
s\ge1:\quad&
v=\frac{s+1}{2s},\quad e=\frac{v}{(1-a)(1+as)},\quad
q=e\,\frac{(1-2a)s-1}{2(1+as)}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The formulas agree at $1$ and give $q(s_*)=0$, $e(s_*)=e_*$, $v(s_*)=v_*$. At each $s\le T$ the bounded cone and frustum coareas and moments agree, and the cap loses $tV_0$. Thus $(P(s)-cC(s))/V_0=\kappa e(s)+1-v(s)-t$. Since $0<t\le(1-2a)^2$, $\kappa$ lies between
$$
\kappa_0=\frac{(1-a)^2}{2-3a},\qquad
\kappa_1=\frac{(1-a)[1-a+(1-2a)^2]}{2-3a}.
$$

For the lower bound, subtract $\kappa-t$ from the corrected cap to get $1-v-\kappa(1-e)$, which is nonnegative for $e\ge1$. Where $e<1$ we have $s>1$, and the quotient
$$
J(s)=\frac{1-v}{1-e}=\frac{(s-1)(1-a)(1+as)}{2a(1-a)s^2+(1-2a)s-1}
$$
is decreasing. In fact let $A=2a(1-a)$, $D=1-2a$ and $E=1-2a+2a^2$. Differentiation gives $J'(s)=-A(Es^2-2Ds+1)/[2(As^2+Ds-1)^2]<0$ by $D^2-E=-A$. The denominator before squaring is strictly increasing for $s>1$, so every $s\le T$ with $e<1$ lies in the same positive-denominator interval as $T$. For $b=1-2a$ and $x=bT-1\ge0$, substituting $t=p/(1+aT)^2$ gives the exact identity
$$
\begin{aligned}
J(T)-\kappa &=
\frac{b(1-b)^2(b+1)Q_b(x)}
 {2(3b+1)[(1-b)x+b+1]^2[(1-b^2)(x^2+1)+2x]},\\
Q_b(x)&=(1-b)^2x^4+[(1-b)^2+4]x^3+(2b^3+b^2+8b+9)x^2\\
&\quad+7(b+1)^2x+2(b+1)^3 .
\end{aligned}
$$
All factors have the displayed nonnegative or positive signs for $0<b<1$, so $J(s)\ge\kappa$ when needed. This proves the lower bound pointwise for $s\le T$.

For the upper bound set $\lambda=(p-\kappa)/(2a-1)$ and $L=v-v_*-\kappa(e-e_*)$. The upper inequality averaged on $[0,T]$ is $\mathbb E L\ge0$, since $\kappa(1+e_*)=v_*+t$. For $s\ge1$, substitution gives
$$
L-\lambda q=\frac{[1-(1-2a)s]^2 Q(s)}
 {4s(a-1)(2a-1)(1+as)^2},\qquad
Q(s)=2a^2(a+2\kappa-1)s+3a^2+4a\kappa-4a-\kappa+1 .
$$
The denominator is positive. At $\kappa_0$, $a+2\kappa_0-1=a(1-a)/(2-3a)>0$, so $Q(s)\ge Q(1)$ over the whole $\kappa$ interval. The affine function $Q(1)$ has endpoint values
$$
\frac{(1-a)(2a^3+5a^2-4a+1)}{2-3a},\qquad
\frac{a(1-a)(16a^3+2a^2-11a+4)}{2-3a}.
$$
The cubics in parentheses have Bernstein coefficient lists $(1,1/3,1/12,1/2)$ and $(4,13/6,1/2,1)$, respectively, in the degree-three Bernstein basis on $b=2a\in[0,1]$. Expansion gives these lists and each coefficient is positive, so $L-\lambda q\ge0$ for $s\ge1$.

For $0\le s\le1$, the residual is affine in $\kappa$. Put $b=2a$, $y=s^2$ and $D=(2a-1)(3a-2)(1-a^2y)^2>0$. Write $B_i^n(u)=\binom{n}{i}u^i(1-u)^{n-i}$. At the endpoints $\kappa_0,\kappa_1$ the exact residuals are
$$
\left.(L-\lambda q)\right|_{\kappa=\kappa_\ell}
=\frac{a^{1+\ell}}{960D}\sum_{i=0}^6\sum_{j=0}^2 A_\ell[i,j] B_i^6(b) B_j^2(y),\qquad \ell=0,1,
$$
with
$$
A_0=\begin{pmatrix}960&480&0\\640&360&80\\384&224&64\\192&111&36\\64&42&32\\0&20&45\\0&30&60\end{pmatrix},\qquad
A_1=\begin{pmatrix}1920&960&0\\1280&800&320\\768&536&336\\384&285&216\\128&116&132\\0&50&110\\0&60&120\end{pmatrix}.
$$
To verify the identities, substitute the small-slope formulas in $D(L-\lambda q)/a^{1+\ell}$ at each endpoint and replace $a$ by $b/2$. This produces a polynomial of degree at most $(6,2)$ in $(b,y)$. A power term $c_{pq}b^py^q$ contributes $c_{pq}\binom{i}{p}\binom{j}{q}/[\binom6p\binom2q]$ to the coefficient at $(i,j)$ when $i\ge p,j\ge q$. Summing gives $A_\ell[i,j]/960$. The coefficient formula follows by expanding $b^p[b+(1-b)]^{6-p}$ and $y^q[y+(1-y)]^{2-q}$. All coefficients are nonnegative, proving $L-\lambda q\ge0$ on this region as well. Averaging over a centered bounded law removes $\lambda q$ and proves the upper bound.

The lower constant at $t=0$ is $\beta_0=v_*/(1+e_*)$, with $\beta_0-4/9=(3a-1)^2/[9(2-3a)]\ge0$. Also $\beta-\beta_0=t(v_*-e_*)/[(1-t)(1+e_*)]\ge0$ since $v_*-e_*=a^2/(1-a)$. The sign of $1/2-\beta$ is the sign of $1-2a-t$, which is nonnegative since $t\le(1-2a)^2$. Thus the infinity record satisfies both inequalities. The bounded representative of f4be2679c83c2fd1 preserves all three records and centers its finite part, so the interval holds for every centered law. Multiplying the lower bound for $\mu$ by $C_\nu$ and the upper bound for $\nu$ by $C_\mu$ and subtracting cancels $c$. The lower pointwise residual vanishes at $s=0$, and the upper one vanishes at $s=s_*$, so this pair attains $\beta$. The zero-coarea conventions and continuity are those of the exact frustum compensation fact f26ba90707244e98, applicable to these separately centered laws with $T\ge1$.

statement:
Let $H>0$ and $0<U<H$, and put $r(z)=(H-z)/(H+1)$ on $[-1,U]$. Use density $1/2$ on the planar region $|x|\le r(z)$. For finite $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and let $C(s),M(s)$ be the integrals of the density and of $z$ times the density over $z+sx=0$ inside the region, with respect to $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Set $a=1/(H+1)$, $T=U/r(U)$, $t=r(U)^2$, $V_0=(H+1)/2$, $V=(1-t)V_0$, $C_0=1-a$ and $p=(1-a)^2$. Assume $0<a<1/2$ and $T\ge s_*=1/(1-2a)$. Set
$$
v_*=1-a,\quad e_*=\frac{1-2a}{1-a},\quad
\kappa=\frac{v_*+t}{1+e_*},\quad
\beta=\frac{\kappa-t}{1-t},\quad
c=\frac{V_0}{C_0}(p-\kappa).
$$
For every probability law on $[0,\infty]$ with averaged moment zero, where $\infty$ has record $(V/2,0,0)$, its averaged records obey $\beta V\le P-cC\le(1-\beta)V$, with $4/9\le\beta\le1/2$. For any two separately centered laws $\mu,\nu$ with $C_\mu+C_\nu>0$, the balanced mean
$$
\frac{C_\nu P_\mu+C_\mu(V-P_\nu)}{V(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
$$
is at least $\beta$. Its value is $1/2$ if one coarea is zero, and it extends continuously as $1/2$ at zero total coarea. The bound $\beta$ is attained by the pair $\delta_0,\delta_{s_*}$.
title: Exact common correction for separately centered planar affine-frustum laws
